# Sprint 1 Video Demonstration — Walkthrough Guide

**Video File:** `sprint1-demonstration.webm` (generated by `npm run test:video`)  
**Test Script:** `tests/e2e/sprint1-demo.video.spec.ts`  
**Duration:** ~28–34 seconds  
**Resolution:** 1280 × 720

This document provides a second-by-second walkthrough of the Sprint 1 Playwright video demonstration.  
Use it to follow along with the recording and understand what each moment demonstrates.

---

## How to Generate the Video

```bash
# Start the database (Docker must be running)
npm run db:up

# Run the video demonstration (starts the app server automatically)
npm run test:video
```

The video is saved to `test-results/sprint1-demo.video-*/video.webm` after the run.

---

## Timestamp Walkthrough

### 00:00 – 00:02 | Application Launch & Sign-In Page

**What you see:** The browser opens the application and navigates to the sign-in page.

**What it verifies:**
- The application is live and reachable (FR-01, AC-01)
- The sign-in form is rendered correctly
- Unauthenticated users land on the login page (not the dashboard)

---

### 00:02 – 00:05 | Requester Login

**What you see:** The email `requester1@macau678.com` and password are entered into the sign-in form and submitted.

**What it verifies:**
- Authentication works for the REQUESTER role (FR-01, AC-01)
- The session is established and the user is redirected to the dashboard
- The dashboard header displays the user's name and REQUESTER role (AC-02)

---

### 00:05 – 00:08 | Requester Dashboard — Empty State & Navigation

**What you see:** The Requester's dashboard is visible. A "New Request" button is present.

**What it verifies:**
- Role-based dashboard renders correctly for REQUESTER (FR-07, AC-08)
- The Requester sees only their own requests (AC-08) — not other users' data
- Navigation controls are available

---

### 00:08 – 00:12 | Create New Purchase Request

**What you see:** The "New Request" button is clicked, the creation form appears, and the following fields are filled in:
- Item Name: `Office Chair - Ergonomic (Video Demo)`
- Quantity: `2`
- Estimated Cost: `12500`
- Justification: `Required for the new team members joining next month.`

**What it verifies:**
- The request creation form renders with all required fields (FR-03, AC-03)
- All four mandatory fields are present and accepting input

---

### 00:12 – 00:14 | Submit the Request

**What you see:** The "Submit" button is clicked. The form disappears and the dashboard or detail page is shown with the new request at status `SUBMITTED`.

**What it verifies:**
- A new request transitions from DRAFT → SUBMITTED on form submit (FR-03, AC-04)
- The request appears on the dashboard with the correct SUBMITTED badge

---

### 00:14 – 00:16 | Sign Out as Requester

**What you see:** The Requester signs out. The page returns to the sign-in screen.

**What it verifies:**
- Sign-out works correctly (FR-01)
- Session is terminated — the app does not retain the authenticated state

---

### 00:16 – 00:19 | Reviewer Login

**What you see:** The email `reviewer1@macau678.com` and password are entered and submitted.

**What it verifies:**
- Authentication works for the REVIEWER role (FR-01, AC-01, AC-02)
- The Reviewer lands on a separate dashboard view

---

### 00:19 – 00:21 | Reviewer Dashboard — Sees Submitted Request

**What you see:** The Reviewer's dashboard shows the SUBMITTED request created by the Requester.

**What it verifies:**
- The Reviewer can see requests assigned to them (FR-07, AC-09)
- The Reviewer does NOT see unrelated users' requests (AC-09)
- Role-based view separation is working

---

### 00:21 – 00:23 | Reviewer Opens Request Detail

**What you see:** The Reviewer clicks on the submitted request. The detail page opens showing:
- Status badge: `SUBMITTED`
- All request fields (item, quantity, cost, justification)
- Approve / Return / Reject action buttons

**What it verifies:**
- Request detail page renders correctly for the REVIEWER role
- All submitted data is preserved (data integrity)
- Reviewer-specific action buttons are present (FR-04, FR-05, AC-05)

---

### 00:23 – 00:24 | Reviewer Returns the Request

**What you see:** The "Return" button is clicked. A reason dialog/field appears. The reason `Please revise the quantity and cost estimate.` is entered and confirmed.

**What it verifies:**
- Return action requires a mandatory reason (BR-05, AC-06)
- The reason field must be non-empty for the action to proceed
- Status changes to `RETURNED` after confirmation (FR-05, AC-07)

---

### 00:24 – 00:26 | Requester Sees Returned Request and Edits It

**What you see:** After re-logging in as the Requester, the returned request appears with status `RETURNED` and the return reason visible. The Requester clicks "Edit" and the form opens pre-populated.

**What it verifies:**
- Returned request is visible to the Requester with the reviewer's reason (AC-07)
- Edit form opens for RETURNED requests (FR-06, AC-07)
- Form is pre-populated with existing field values (not blank)
- Edit is NOT available for APPROVED/REJECTED requests (BR-06, BR-07)

---

### 00:26 – 00:28 | Resubmit and Audit History

**What you see:** Fields are updated. The "Resubmit" button is clicked. The request returns to `SUBMITTED` status. The audit history / timeline section is scrolled into view, showing:
- `CREATED`
- `SUBMITTED`
- `RETURNED`
- `RESUBMITTED`

**What it verifies:**
- Resubmission transitions the request back to SUBMITTED (FR-06, AC-07)
- Full audit history is maintained and displayed (AC-11)
- Each history entry includes the action, actor, and timestamp

## UAT Test Case Coverage

| Timestamp | UAT Test Case | Path Verified |
|-----------|--------------|---------------|
| 00:00–00:05 | UAT-TC-01 (partial) | Authentication (AC-01, AC-02) |
| 00:05–00:14 | UAT-TC-01 | Submit request, SUBMITTED state (AC-03, AC-04) |
| 00:16–00:23 | UAT-TC-01 | Reviewer sees and opens request (AC-05, AC-09) |
| 00:23–00:24 | UAT-TC-02 (partial) | Mandatory return reason (BR-05, AC-06) |
| 00:24–00:26 | UAT-TC-04 | Edit returned request (FR-06, AC-07) |
| 00:26–00:28 | UAT-TC-04 | Resubmit + audit history (AC-07, AC-11) |

> [!NOTE]
> UAT-TC-03 (forbidden access) and UAT-TC-05 (terminal state immutability) involve
> access-denial scenarios that are best verified manually per the instructions in `UAT_TEST_CASES.md`.
> These cannot be cleanly shown in a linear video flow.

---

## Notes for Reviewers

- The video is generated from an automated Playwright test, not a manual screen recording.
- All interactions (typing, clicking, navigation) are performed by Playwright in a real browser.
- The test script (`tests/e2e/sprint1-demo.video.spec.ts`) serves as executable documentation — each step is commented with the AC/BR it verifies.
- The video demonstrates the **happy path** and the **return/edit/resubmit** cycle. Edge cases (boundary validation, access denial) are covered by the remaining test cases in `UAT_TEST_CASES.md`.
